goal: Make Entroly the most discoverable, verifiable, installable, and independently evaluable open-source context-assurance project.

states.strong: A maintained repository-owned surface exists, is tested or release-gated, and has clear user value.
states.partial: A useful surface exists but coverage, evidence, external reach, or maintenance is incomplete.
states.gap: The dimension is relevant but lacks a sufficient maintained surface.
states.blocked: Completion requires external infrastructure, third-party acceptance, or platform-specific evidence that is not yet available.
states.published: A third-party surface is visibly published and recorded with a proof URL.

leadership_rule: Entroly may call a dimension leading only when its evidence is current, reproducible where applicable, broader or more trustworthy than named alternatives, and independently reviewable. Coverage alone is not leadership.

dimensions.name: Category positioning
dimensions.leadership_target: Own the Context Assurance category with one consistent definition across every package, registry, document, and external listing.
dimensions.next_action: Keep Context Assurance as the primary category and Context OS as the architectural explanation; prevent tagline drift in release checks.

dimensions.name: Repository first impression
dimensions.leadership_target: A new visitor understands the problem, trust model, install path, proof, and limitations in under two minutes.
dimensions.next_action: Continuously validate badges, install commands, proof artifacts, and the first-screen message.

dimensions.name: Python registry distribution
dimensions.leadership_target: Best-in-category PyPI metadata, fresh wheels, clear extras, Python 3.10-3.14 support, and tested pure-Python fallback.
dimensions.next_action: Keep package metadata, docs URLs, optional dependencies, and release versions synchronized.

dimensions.name: Node and npm distribution
dimensions.leadership_target: Node, WASM, npm CLI, and MCP users receive the same core contract and current install instructions as Python users.
dimensions.next_action: Keep the primary `entroly` package, MCP bridge, WASM exports, docs, and version checks aligned.

dimensions.name: Rust and native distribution
dimensions.leadership_target: One audited native engine with reproducible Rust, Python, WASM, and single-binary proxy behavior.
dimensions.next_action: Maintain Clippy, native tests, offline build evidence, and cross-surface conformance.

dimensions.name: Homebrew distribution
dimensions.leadership_target: Release-synchronized Homebrew installation with verified source checksum and a clean-machine smoke test.
dimensions.next_action: Continue deriving formula URL and checksum from the released PyPI source artifact.

dimensions.name: Container distribution
dimensions.leadership_target: Documented and tested container use for CLI, MCP, and proxy modes with explicit persistence and network boundaries.
dimensions.next_action: Add container-specific user journeys when public usage shows recurring configuration errors.

dimensions.name: MCP discovery and registries
dimensions.leadership_target: Current manifests and verified listings across major MCP catalogs, with scoped roots, bounded outputs, and security documentation.
dimensions.next_action: Submit the prepared catalog entries and record public PR or listing URLs before changing status.

dimensions.name: Claude plugin and Agent Skill visibility
dimensions.leadership_target: Native Claude plugin metadata, managed instructions, Agent Skill documentation, and presence in Claude-specific catalogs.
dimensions.next_action: Validate the installed Claude experience end to end and submit to the prepared Claude catalogs.

dimensions.name: Agent and IDE integration breadth
dimensions.leadership_target: Every claimed integration has an explicit path, bounded support status, installation instructions, and conformance evidence.
dimensions.next_action: Convert compatibility claims into executable journeys wherever the host can be installed in CI.

dimensions.name: One-command onboarding and verification
dimensions.leadership_target: A user can install, configure, verify, simulate value, inspect privacy boundaries, and undo changes without reading internal architecture docs.
dimensions.next_action: Add a generated integration prompt and reversible setup summary for every supported host.

dimensions.name: Owned documentation depth
dimensions.leadership_target: Task-specific pages for installation, integrations, security, benchmarks, troubleshooting, architecture, and limitations.
dimensions.next_action: Keep the documentation information architecture concise and add pages only when they answer a distinct user query.

dimensions.name: Technical SEO
dimensions.leadership_target: Canonical URLs, accurate metadata, structured data, sitemap coverage, stable titles, and crawlable task-specific pages.
dimensions.next_action: Generate sitemap entries from the published-page inventory and fail CI when indexed pages or canonical URLs drift.

dimensions.name: AEO, GEO, and machine-readable discovery
dimensions.leadership_target: Search and answer engines can retrieve direct, caveated answers about product fit, privacy, integrations, recovery, and limitations.
dimensions.next_action: Add machine-readable citation and release metadata, then test important direct answers for drift.

dimensions.name: Multilingual discovery
dimensions.leadership_target: High-quality maintained pages and catalog entries for major developer languages, beginning with Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, and Portuguese.
dimensions.next_action: Start with concise installation and trust-boundary pages; require native or expert review before publication.

dimensions.name: Comparison and buyer evaluation
dimensions.leadership_target: Help users choose among Entroly, raw context, and alternatives through reproducible criteria rather than rank claims.
dimensions.next_action: Publish a workload-selection guide covering recovery, proxy behavior, content types, latency, trust, integration, and total-session impact.

dimensions.name: Independent hands-on reviews
dimensions.leadership_target: Multiple independent reviews with raw commands, pinned versions, real tasks, task outcomes, token usage, failures, recovery, and receipts.
dimensions.next_action: Recruit technically independent reviewers for Claude Code debugging, structured-data compression, conversation compaction, and matched-budget agent tasks.

dimensions.name: Neutral external benchmark participation
dimensions.leadership_target: Version-pinned adapters in independent harnesses with unchanged workloads, control arms, raw artifacts, and quality-plus-cost reporting.
dimensions.next_action: Complete adapters only after upstream protocols are frozen; never tune on held-out outcomes.

dimensions.name: Curated lists and developer directories
dimensions.leadership_target: Accurate placement in the highest-signal Claude, MCP, Rust, LLMOps, local-AI, CLI, and agent-infrastructure catalogs.
dimensions.next_action: Submit priority targets one at a time and monitor merged wording for stale commands or claims.

dimensions.name: Operating-system package managers
dimensions.leadership_target: Maintained Nix, Scoop, FreeBSD, and additional platform packages with reproducible artifacts and update automation.
dimensions.next_action: Produce target-platform smoke evidence before requesting inclusion.

dimensions.name: Launch channels
dimensions.leadership_target: Evidence-bounded launch packages for Show HN, Product Hunt, relevant developer communities, and release-specific announcements.
dimensions.next_action: Verify the released package and publish one technical launch at a time, then record public URLs and outcomes.

dimensions.name: Newsletters, podcasts, and technical media
dimensions.leadership_target: Earn recurring independent coverage by providing reproducible stories, not paid or copied announcements.
dimensions.next_action: Pitch technically relevant editors and reviewers around exact recovery, Context Receipts, neutral benchmarks, and local verification.

dimensions.name: Community and social proof
dimensions.leadership_target: Visible user stories, integration contributions, benchmark reproduction reports, and responsive issue handling.
dimensions.next_action: Collect permissioned user stories and reproducibility reports while preserving failures and conflict disclosures.

dimensions.name: Release communication and changelog visibility
dimensions.leadership_target: Every meaningful release has concise user-facing notes, migration guidance, trustworthy evidence, and channel-specific summaries.
dimensions.next_action: Generate release announcement drafts from a reviewed manifest and publish only after package availability is verified.

dimensions.name: Research and citation metadata
dimensions.leadership_target: CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, stable benchmark artifact identifiers, and research-friendly methodology documentation.
dimensions.next_action: Add citation files to the release version-synchronization contract and introduce stable artifact identifiers when a public dataset archive is created.

dimensions.name: Press and media kit
dimensions.leadership_target: Approved descriptions, logos, screenshots, project facts, claim rules, and reproducible demo commands in one maintained location.
dimensions.next_action: Keep media assets and approved facts synchronized with releases and reject invented customer, company, funding, or adoption claims.

dimensions.name: Security, privacy, and trust visibility
dimensions.leadership_target: The clearest privacy boundary, threat model, fail-closed behavior, recovery integrity, dependency audit, and vulnerability reporting in the category.
dimensions.next_action: Keep security claims tied to executable checks and document residual risks for proxy, MCP, local stores, and generated configuration.

dimensions.name: Governance and contributor experience
dimensions.leadership_target: Clear contribution paths for product code, integrations, benchmarks, documentation, translations, and distribution maintenance.
dimensions.next_action: Add ownership and review requirements for externally visible metadata, integrations, benchmark adapters, and translations.

dimensions.name: Extension and addon ecosystem
dimensions.leadership_target: A safe extension contract with discoverable community integrations, explicit permissions, version compatibility, and uninstall behavior.
dimensions.next_action: Define a checksum-verifiable addon manifest and explicit permission model before promoting a community registry.

dimensions.name: Distribution observability and maintenance
dimensions.leadership_target: One dashboard and CI contract for every package, catalog, listing, docs page, launch asset, benchmark adapter, and external proof URL.
dimensions.next_action: Add periodic freshness checks for published third-party proof URLs and package-registry availability without turning transient outages into false failures.
